subject: On-Prem Hostname Trust Model & Proxy Delegation — Case Study

Subject: Private deployment: hostname delegation and TLS termination options

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're about to finalize an on-prem rollout for our test cluster and need a short, concrete recommendation for hostname assertion, cert ownership, and where TLS should terminate. Our constraints:
- Network egress is heavily restricted (no public ACME calls from hosts).
- We must maintain auditable proof of trust mapping for SOC2 (who owns which FQDN).
- Some downstream clients expect a customer-controlled SAN on the cert.

Could Redwood provide 2 recommended patterns (one minimal change, one locked-down enterprise) and a quick list of operational steps? If you can share a sample CSR or comms template for DNS proof, that'd help procurement.

Appreciate it — Arun

--
Arun Patel
Head of Platform, FinReg Systems
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Arun Patel <arun.patel@finreg.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: hostname delegation and TLS termination options

Arun —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Attached is a short case study and two recommended patterns tailored to your environment. High level:

1) Bridge-mode (minimal change) — Redwood-managed certs, customer controls DNS ownership assertions via TXT proofs. TLS terminates at the Redwood private proxy in the VPC; backend traffic uses mTLS with our ephemeral client certs. Pros: fast onboarding, lower ops burden. Cons: customer needs to accept Redwood as termination boundary; requires documented DNS proof workflow for audit.

2) Brokered-host model (enterprise/locked-down) — Customer owns host certs issued by their internal PKI; Redwood runs a pass-through proxy that performs SNI routing but does not terminate customer certs. TLS termination happens at the customer-managed edge; Redwood validates client certs using a pinned trust bundle. Pros: maximal control and auditability. Cons: higher ops (certificate rotation coordination, offline CSR exchange).

Operational steps (short):
- Inventory FQDNs and map to service owners (spreadsheet attached).
- Choose pattern: Bridge-mode = faster; Brokered-host = compliance-first.
- Exchange proof-of-ownership: TXT record for Bridge-mode OR signed CSR bundle for Brokered-host (csr-example.txt attached).
- Onboarding runbook: verification window, cert pin storage, rotation cadence, and emergency rollback MOP (see onprem-rollout-mop.xlsx).

I included Marissa and Karthik for technical specifics and a suggested rollout schedule. If you want, we can run a 60-minute case-call next week and model the sprint tasks for procurement and security.

-Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Arun / team —

Adding a few low-level notes from infra SRE perspective (attached: 2027-06-18_finreg-hostname-trust-design.pdf):
- For Bridge-mode we recommend a short lived wildcard cert on the Redwood proxy (7–14 days) combined with our KV prefix cache so we can renew without touching customer infra. This reduces token exposure while keeping audit logs for each renewal.
- For Brokered-host model, we need a consistent CSR metadata format (see csr-example.txt). Important fields: fqdn, owner-email, intended-validity, and key-usage flags. We use an internal signing queue (HSM-backed) and return signed bundles via the private control plane.
- DNS proof: prefer TXT with a predictable prefix (redwood-verif=sha256:...) to make audits reproducible. FinReg should keep change control records in their ticketing system; we'll attach the verification timestamp in our onboarding artifact.

Operational caveat: if you choose Brokered-host and your edge can't initiate outbound ACME, we'll coordinate offline signing windows and a backup renewal operator. That increases lead time by ~2 business days per rotation.

Next step: pick a pattern. If Bridge-mode, provide the DNS zone admin and a ballooned list (10–20 initial FQDNs) and we will open a one-week pilot. If Brokered-host, we'll schedule a rotation dry-run with staged CSR exchange.

-Marissa

Attachments: 2027-06-18_finreg-hostname-trust-design.pdf
